question.text: When an option buyer exercises a call option, the option writer is:

answer.text: Legally bound to sell the underlying at the strike price to the buyer
Free to choose whether to honor the contract or not
Entitled to receive the premium amount again from the buyer
Required to buy the underlying from the buyer at the strike price

explanation.text: The Logic: The option writer has the obligation in the contract. When the buyer decides to exercise a call option, the writer is legally bound to sell the underlying at the strike price. The writer earned the premium upfront as compensation for bearing this obligation. The buyer exercises only when it is favorable (ITM), so the writer faces a potential loss. The Trap: The writer cannot choose whether to honor the contract — the obligation is binding. No additional premium is paid upon exercise. For a call option, the writer SELLS (not buys) to the buyer. The writer's risk is that the underlying price goes much higher than the strike.
